sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Out-of-Gauge (OOG) Heavy Industrial Project Cargo Logistics

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (code-based company and commercial law; Islamic Sharia limited to personal-status matters; regulatory dualism between the Companies Act Law No. 194 of 2020, the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, and the Money Laundering Act Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 13 March 1996, in force 1996)
Egypt-UK Promotion and Protection of Investment Treaty (1975; continued application confirmed by 1976 exchange of notes)
Egypt-US Bilateral Investment Treaty (1986; amended by protocol of 16 March 1999)
Egypt-China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 13 March 1997, applied since 1999)
Egypt-EU Association Agreement (2004, in force; investment promotion and customs cooperation provisions applicable)
Greater Arab Free Trade Area (GAFTA) membership for regional logistics and transit corridors

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 31 of 2014 and Law No. 181 of 2022; Executive Regulations of the AML Law (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2003, as amended, particularly UBO identification duties referencing Article 3); Egyptian Companies Act Law No. 194 of 2020, Articles 22, 26 and 27 (obligation to maintain a register of ultimate beneficial owners); Executive Regulations of the Companies Act (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 2022); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; terrorist-asset freezing and listing rules under Law No. 8 of 2015 and notices published by the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EGFIU); GAFI one-stop-shop UBO declaration forms integrated into the company formation workflow.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / certificate of existence of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry or Registrar of Companies of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention): Notary Public in country of origin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of country of origin, then Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board or shareholder resolution of each foreign shareholder authorizing incorporation of an Egyptian LLC and appointing the UBO nominees
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization with the same three-step chain as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the bio-page of the passport of each foreign manager and each foreign ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the passport-issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian legal representative or the GAFI one-stop-shop formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the principal's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn certified Arabic translation of all legalized foreign documents and notarized geopolitical certified copies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed legal translator registered with the Egyptian Court of Appeals, certified by the Translation Department of the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs countersignature and notarial seal in Egypt

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all founders, managers, authorized signatories and UBOs holding 25% or more against: (i) the national terrorist list and terrorist-entity notices published by the Egyptian Public Prosecutor and the EGFIU; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) the OFAC SDN and related non-SDN lists; (iv) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (v) domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Person (PEP) databases, with enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval for PEP transactions under Article 3 of Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended; screening results must be documented in the GAFI-compliant client-acceptance file and continuously monitored after formation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Invest Easy platform (https://investinegypt.gov.eg) - name-reservation step within the Start Business workflow; ultimate entry into the Commercial Registry administered by GAFI in coordination with the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be written in Arabic script under Article 93 of Law No. 194 of 2020; a Latin-script transliteration may be registered as a secondary trade or style name, but the Arabic name prevails for registration, banking, and lien purposes and must be clearly distinct from all existing Arabic and Latin-registered names as verified by the GAFI Commercial Registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Insurance, Reinsurance, Securities, Investment Fund (require prior CBE or FRA licensed authorization and are unavailable to an unlicensed LLC)
Egypt, Arab Republic of Egypt, Republic, President, Armed Forces, Police (state-reserved and prohibited)
National, Governmental, Ministry, Authority, Holdings (require prior ministerial or GAFI specific authorization; Holdings additionally requires the special holding-company structure)
Any token implying a public institution, religious reference contrary to public order, or a misleading connection to public sector activities
Solely foreign-script names without a mandatory Arabic form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days of an electronic name-rejection notice, submit a written reconsideration request to the GAFI Name Approval Committee with amended name variants. If reconsideration is refused, file a formal administrative appeal (tazallum) with the GAFI Board Grievance Committee attaching the name-clearance reference, the stated rejection grounds, and pre-search or trademark evidence; the Grievance Committee must issue a decision within 30 days. A further negative decision may be challenged before the Administrative Court (Al-Mahkama Al-Idariyya) of the Council of State within 60 days of notification. The name reservation is renewable once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the applicable renewal fee before the base window lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are tolerated at the registration stage only if a verifiable Egyptian address is designated for the registered office, official mail reception, and tax-inspection service of process within the Commercial Registry format; for a project-cargo logistics vehicle seeking Milestone Wire and Letter of Credit facilities, the banking AML review will in practice require physical-tenant evidence or a formal sub-office agreement rather than a bare virtual postbox.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 10% to 15% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection of the administrative registered office for a standard-risk LLC; the Egyptian Tax Authority and labor authorities mainly perform on-site premise checks when VAT, customs, heavy-lift equipment imports, or foreign-employment ratio anomalies are flagged, while warehouse and project job sites attract materially higher inspection attention than the legal seat.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory name clearance and reservation fee for three name variants
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory GAFI tariff schedule (Egyptian pound basket inclusive of electronic payment surcharge)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation filing composite - LLC memorandum of association, UBO disclosure form, commercial registry entry, legal entity number, and tax-card linkage
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GAFI one-stop shop with EGFIU-linked UBO register entry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory composite tariff under Law No. 194 of 2020 and GAFI fee schedule, including electronic formation stamping

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the memorandum of association and certified formation minutes before the Egyptian Notary Public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Justice - Notary Public offices
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff under Law No. 68 of 1947 scaled to authorized capital with statutory minimum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of four foreign corporate and identity document bundles (origin-country MFA authentication, Egyptian Embassy or Consulate legalization, Egyptian MFA counter-legalization)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Egyptian diplomatic or consular mission abroad, and Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Authentication Department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee schedule, approximately USD 200 per document bundle with a USD 150 to 350 range depending on the mission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified legal translation into Arabic of all legalized foreign documents (approximately 10 pages) with Egyptian MFA translation-department certification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed legal translator registered with the Egyptian Court of Appeals and Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Translation Department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 20 to 40 per standard legal page plus MFA certification stamps

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name certificate, certified Arabic formation certificate copies, and official corporate seal procurement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GAFI, Notary Public, and licensed seal engraver
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory copy-certification fees plus market cost of the corporate chop

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address package for 12 months - Cairo or Alexandria business-services center with mail handling and statutory-notice reception
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 100 per month plus deposit for a premium-grade registered seat in a commercial district

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions database screening, and AML/CFT client-acceptance file for three UBO positions across multiple lists
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global sanctions and PEP data provider (LexisNexis or World-Check class) supervised by Egyptian compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per automated screening bundle per screened subject under Article 3 of the AML Law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External legal counsel - pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO ownership-tracing report, name strategy, investment treaty and DTA eligibility memo, and formation-closing opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee engagement benchmark of USD 2,000 to 2,800 for a standard-risk LLC formation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank-readiness file for Milestone Wire and Letter of Credit - pre-account structure memorandum with UBO declarations formatted for Egyptian banking AML documentation and tax-card preliminaries
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian law firm with local big-four advisory desk
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark add-on to the formation engagement; excludes bank account opening and bank fees which are post-incorporation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, particularly Articles 102–128 (Limited Liability Companies); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 Articles 19–23; Executive Regulations issued under the Companies Law
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Incorporation and Commercial Registration Department / One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in Arabic, together with the standard GAFI incorporation application form for limited liability companies
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an LLC under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; however, the capital must be fully subscribed in the Articles of Association, founders must contribute the stated capital before registration, and cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank certificate or held in a temporary escrow account at an Egyptian bank until the Certificate of Incorporation is issued. In-kind contributions must be valued and described in the MOA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the first meeting of the board of managers of EG_LLC held at its registered office: (1) the subscription to the company's share capital by the founding members is approved and confirmed; (2) the registered office and principal place of business stated in the Articles of Association is adopted for statutory and fiscal purposes; (3) [Name] is appointed chairman and managing director, [Name] vice-chairman, and [Name] company secretary for the first statutory term; (4) the managing director is authorized to sign, submit, and correct all filing instruments with GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Egyptian Tax Authority; and (5) all objective steps and expenditures necessary for completion of incorporation, physical licensing, and opening of bank facilities are ratified. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Legal Form Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Online Investor Platform / Investor Services Center (One-Stop Shop)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the GAFI e-service portal, select 'Company Name Reservation', and submit up to three Arabic and Latin name alternatives in the prescribed format. Pay the reservation invoice electronically. Use the validated name in all subsequent constitutional documents; the reservation remains valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Founders' passport or national ID copies
Power of attorney if submitted by an incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, prohibited wording, or conflict, file an administrative objection to the GAFI Name Committee; alternatively resubmit amended name alternatives without waiving the search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Approval, and Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public Offices and an Egyptian attorney licensed before the Court of Cassation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare an Arabic-language Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association for the limited liability company, stating the ISIC 5229 project cargo and heavy-haul logistics object, capital structure, shareholder quotas, board of managers' powers, and meeting thresholds. Convene a founders' meeting to approve the instrument and authenticate all founder signatures before a notary public.
required_dossiers: Draft MOA and AOA in Arabic
Lease contract or address authorization for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies missing provisions or inconsistencies, correct the draft, have all founders re-sign and re-attest, and obtain GAFI Technical Office approval before resubmission for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Funding Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary subscription account in the name of EG_LLC before issuance of the commercial register, deposit the subscribed capital in cash, or deliver an equivalent in-kind valuation report. Obtain a bank certificate evidencing full funding for submission with the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Founders' resolution and name approval certificate
Passports or national IDs and tax identification numbers of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence for heavy-project logistics, provide a written business purpose statement and customer list; if funds are not accepted, restructure the deposit arrangement or substitute an in-kind valuation certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Dossier to GAFI and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Corporate Registration Department / One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation dossier physically at the competent GAFI investment branch or upload it through the investor portal. Pay the registration fee and stamp duties, obtain an acknowledgment of filing, and allow GAFI to verify statutory conditions for LLC formation. GAFI issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the initial Commercial Registry extract.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues an inquiry or rejection, cure the cited deficiency within 15 business days using the comments notice; changes to capital, object, or managers require a new founders' resolution and re-notarization before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry, Tax, Social Insurance, and Municipal Post-Incorporation Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop desks for the Commercial Registry, Egyptian Tax Authority, and National Organization for Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, obtain the Commercial Registry extract, electronic tax card and tax identification number, VAT registration where applicable or when voluntary registration is elected, and social insurance registration. Initiate coordination with the local civil defense office for premises clearance in later physical licensing.
required_dossiers: Initial board resolution appointing officers and bank signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Egyptian Tax Authority or NOSI flags missing declarations, file the relevant nil or opening registration forms online; if the Commercial Registry requires additional notarized pages, obtain them from the notary and refile at the same GAFI window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance File, Official Seal, and Bank Signature Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: EG_LLC management and a Central Bank of Egypt-regulated commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, adopt the minute book and share register, approve the corporate seal where required, and prepare the bank signature card. Open the operational bank account for milestone wires and letters of credit, requiring dual signatory authorization per the board resolution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires a separate board banking resolution for letters of credit or international wire facilities, adopt an ad hoc resolution at the next board meeting; certified copies of governance documents may be notarized or apostilled as conditions require.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Roads, Bridges and Land Transport (GARBLT) – Land Freight Transport Licensing Directorate, Ministry of Transport
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Road Transport Operator License for Heavy and Out-of-Gauge Project Cargo Freight Services under Law No. 12 of 1996; route-specific oversized-load Non-Objection Certificates are also required for each GARBLT heavy-haul movement

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Limited Environmental Impact Assessment / Initial Environmental Review for logistics and heavy-cargo storage facilities; operations involving substantial vehicle maintenance, fueling, or hazardous material storage may be escalated to Category C requiring a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 and Ministerial Decree No. 44 of 2000: the diesel fleet must meet ambient air and mobile-source emission limits; wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must not exceed pH 6–9.5, TSS 20 mg/L, oil and grease 15 mg/L, and applicable COD/BOD thresholds; above-ground fuel storage above 250 liters requires double containment and a spill response plan; used oils and contaminated waste must be handled through licensed waste contractors with EEAA manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Egyptian Civil Defense Authority under Law No. 12 of 1961 for the registered premises, warehouses, and laydown areas; structural load inspection certification for heavy-lift platforms and mobile crane operating zones; occupational safety and health clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003, including PPE compliance, load-securement supervision, and heavy-lift operator certificates.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance - official revenue administration; registration and filing via ETA electronic tax platform at https://www.eta.gov.eg (integrated e-invoice, e-receipt and e-filing portal).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The EG_LLC is incorporated in Egypt and must obtain its statutory Tax Card (TIN) from the Egyptian Tax Authority after incorporation. Procedure: (1) register the entity with GAFI and obtain the Commercial Registry certificate; (2) submit ETA Tax Card Registration (Form 11) online or at the competent tax office, attaching Commercial Registry certificate, articles of association, lease/evidence of business premises, identity documents of legal representatives, and initial bank account details; (3) ETA validates the application and issues the Tax Card bearing the TIN. (4) Separately file VAT registration with ETA under Law 67/2016 once annual taxable supplies reach or are expected to exceed EGP 500,000, attaching the Tax Card, activity description, and estimated turnover; ETA verifies and issues the VAT registration certificate. Foreign ownership does not change or bypass these domestic registration steps.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An Egyptian-registered LLC is a resident juridical person subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income under Law 91 of 2005; pass-through treatment is unavailable for LLC shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a check-the-box classification and has no domestic hybrid mismatch election. Elective mechanisms are limited to: (a) consolidated corporate income tax filing for resident companies with a 95% or greater direct/indirect holding relationship; and (b) simplified or cash-basis VAT accounting for taxpayers within ETA-affirmed small turnover thresholds. Foreign-owned LLCs cannot elect fiscal transparency.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Egyptian Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 (as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies of goods and services; mandatory registration applies once turnover reaches or is anticipated to reach that threshold. Non-resident suppliers carrying on taxable activities through a fixed establishment in Egypt or otherwise required to collect Egyptian VAT must register under the same threshold; supplies by foreign suppliers without an Egyptian fixed establishment are generally subject to reverse-charge by the resident recipient.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: ETA mandates e-invoicing and e-receipt transmission under Ministerial Decrees 188 of 2020 and 623 of 2021. Taxpayers must issue invoices in JSON/XML format, apply digital signatures and QR encodings, and transmit them in near real-time to ETA's e-tax platform via official APIs. ETA performs fiscal clearance and validation by returning a unique invoice ID before the invoice may lawfully be used by the customer. e-Receipts are similarly cleared for retail B2C transactions. Export supplies are integrated into the same e-invoice pipeline; late, altered or unauthorized transmission attracts per-document fines and suspension of e-tax credentials.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported outside Egypt are zero-rated under VAT Law 67/2016 where the applicant is a VAT registered exporter, the Egyptian Customs Export Declaration proves departure from Egyptian customs territory, the commercial invoice reflects arm's length terms, and the foreign currency proceeds are received in Egypt through a licensed bank within 180 days of export. Zero rating extends to directly connected project cargo and heavy haul logistics services where the service is performed in relation to export cargo or performed outside Egypt for a non-resident customer. Unused input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is eligible for refund under ETA export-refund instructions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Egyptian Customs Export Declaration (ACK form and customs statistical summary)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / transport contract evidencing departure from Egyptian ports, airports or border crossings
Inward remittance certificate / foreign currency bank credit advice establishing export proceeds credited to an Egyptian bank account
Commercial export invoice together with the foreign purchase order or export contract
ETA e-invoice and VAT return schedule identifying the exported supplies as zero-rated
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA cross-validates zero-rated claims through customs export data, e-invoice transmission records and banking foreign-currency credit instruments. Failure to satisfy the export conditions, including non-repatriation of proceeds within 180 days or submission of deficient documentation, causes the supply to be retrospectively re-rated at 14% VAT; any input VAT refund already granted is clawed back and assessed together with monthly late-payment interest under the VAT Law. Fraudulent or forged export documentation constitutes VAT evasion and is subject to criminal penalties including imprisonment of up to five years and fines between EGP 10,000 and EGP 50,000, in addition to full tax and penalty readjustment; responsible officers of the LLC may also be made jointly liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), operating under Law No. 194 of 2020 regarding the Central Bank and Banking System, together with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) for FDI registration and the Ministry of Investment. All foreign exchange operations must be conducted through CBE-licensed authorized banks, and the CBE maintains supervisory authority over balance of payments reporting, inward/outward remittance coding, and hedging eligibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a liberalized managed-float regime following the March 2024 exchange-rate unification; the Egyptian Pound (EGP) is effectively fully convertible for current-account transactions (trade in goods and services, dividend remittances, loan repayments) and for documented capital-account transactions, subject to CBE submitted forms. Foreign shareholders may repatriate dividends and sale proceeds in the same currency brought in, provided the underlying investment is registered with GAFI and the CBE and tax clearances (Egyptian Tax Authority Form 11 for dividend remittance) are obtained. No separate 'foreign investment approval' is required for LLC formation since non-resident ownership is fully allowed, but each inward and outward remittance requires purpose-code declaration and a CBE-compliant bank transaction slip. Capital-account outflows (loan repayments, intercompany loans) face higher evidentiary scrutiny and may be subordinated to tax registration certificates, audited financial statements, and CBE prior approval for EUR-denominated supplier payments exceeding 50,000 EUR or equivalent (Notification requirement for commercial registration of import operations is handled via the bank). Profit repatriation hurdles remain procedural rather than quantitative: the entity must evidence that (i) the dividend was declared from distributable reserves audited by a CPA licensed in Egypt, (ii) corporate income tax, stamp tax, and capital gains tax liabilities have been settled or tax clearance obtained, and (iii) the CBE Form for Outward Remittance—Profit Repatriation is countersigned by the authorized dealer bank. For out-of-gauge project-cargo logistics, freight receivables from international clients are treated as current-account export proceeds and enjoy free convertibility; no residual controls, waiting periods, or qouta approvals apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export and service-trade proceeds must be repatriated within 180 days from the date of shipment for goods, or from the contractual invoice due date for services, and credited to an account maintained at an authorized dealer bank in Egypt. The CBE's current framework (as harmonized after Circular No. 204/2022 and subsequent 2023-2024 relaxations) does not impose a mandatory EGP conversion ratio on non-commodity exporters; proceeds may be retained in eligible foreign-currency accounts (Retained FX Account / Export Proceeds Sub-Account), but the bank must receive a 'Proceeds Utilization Instruction' within 14 days of credit. Generically, for goods exporters the CBE retains the power to reinstate a partial conversion requirement (historically up to 50%) under exceptional liquidity stress, whereas for freight/logistics service exporters that power is exercised only through written CBE directive and has not been activated. Exporters of OOG heavy-haul services (transport, handling, crane and lashing operations, customs representation) must submit the Service Export Declaration in electronic form through the authorized bank with a copy of the signed service agreement, invoice, bank transaction advice, and proof of physical completion (CBM, bill of lading, project milestone certificate) to evidence the 180-day repatriation timeline. Failure to repatriate within the statutory window exposes the LLC to a fine of up to EGP 50,000 under Exchange Control Regulations and to audit adjustments by the Egyptian Tax Authority; mitigated by applying in writing to CBE for a one-time extension prior to the deadline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (for paid-in capital under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017) and Operational Account
Operational Account + FCY Retained Revenue Account
Operational Account with Trade Finance Line (LC/MT103) and FX Hedging Facility
Operational Account for Government-Tied Logistics Contracts and Bonded Cargo Transactions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low—legally non-viable as a core treasury rail. Under the Central Bank of Egypt's Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and its prior licensing circulars, any payment service provider, electronic wallet operator, or cross-border EMI acting as an account-holding institution for an Egyptian-domiciled corporate must obtain a CBE license and maintain a local establishment. Offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise, Payoneer, Mercury, etc.) cannot hold KYC accounts for Egyptian LLCs nor issue account/routing details for sovereign-required FX repatriation. They may be used only as auxiliary receivable collection channels for small milestone deposits under USD 5,000 from overseas counterparties, but the funds must then be swept into the Egyptian banking account via MT103; direct settlement of project-cargo invoices through offshore EMIs is prohibited and would breach the service-export repatriation window. The LLC must therefore maintain its principal transaction accounts with CBE-licensed banks; any use of unlicensed EMIs is an AML red flag.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Egyptian resident LLCs with any non-resident shareholder, the authorized signatory/manager must attend an in-branch KYC interview and customer-due-diligence session. CBE e-KYC rules permit remote document collection for low-risk account openings under bank discretion, but in practice tier-1 banks require physical presentation of the original commercial registration, power-of-attorney, share certificate ledger, and valid national ID/passport for first activation and for issuance of internet-banking credentials for FCY-account operations. For the EG_LLC—engaged in heavy-haul logistics and thus classified Low_Risk_Standard by the AML risk hierarchy—the following mandates apply: (a) the legal representative (Egyptian manager) must attend in person for biometric verification; (b) each non-resident shareholder whose ownership exceeds 25% must either appear physically at the bank in Egypt or complete a notarized and Apostilled signature certification at an Egyptian consulate, which is then accepted; (c) at minimum one board-level interview with the AML Compliance Officer is required to map the transport-chain business model; (d) remote submission of scanned due-diligence files is permitted only in the pre-screening phase, not as substitute for the interview. Failure to complete the physical-first signing protocol will leave the account in a 'pending activation' status and block all FX operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: chain of shareholder entities domiciled in multi-jurisdiction freight-holding structures (UAE, Cyprus, BVI) with nominee layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI/CBE-compliant Beneficial Ownership Register excerpt confirming ultimate natural persons; memorandum of association; shareholder register and nominal ledger; notarized statutory declaration of control; financial statement consolidation from ultimate parent; bank reference letters from the first-layer correspondent bank; corporate registry certificates (Apostilled and translated) for each intermediate holding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flag: invoice for transport/logistics services materially out of line with cargo dimensions, weight, or route profile, or invoice to a freight-forwarder rather than the beneficial shipper/consignee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contract and Incoterms sheet; Bill of Lading/Air Waybill with gross weight and CBM reconciliation; yard receipt and out-of-gauge survey report; crane/stevedoring and lashing certificates; road-permit documentation for abnormal loads; bank purpose-code declaration and underlying invoice; egyptian Customs export/import declaration (if any); photo/video evidence of load and delivery with geotag timestamp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list exposure: cargo transshipment call at a high-risk port (e.g., a vessel route touching a sanctioned country or loading equipment of Russian/Chinese origin feared to be defense-adjacent).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level OFAC/UN/EU/UK/CBE and consolidated Egyptian AML blacklist screening certificates; beneficial-owner passport/ID copies; end-user/importer attestation with CTH (contractor's letter of control); vessel/aircarrier IMO or call-sign report showing no flag or owner on sanctioned lists; independent sanctions-screening log for each counterparty including freight prepayment lenders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structurally high-value forward-payment with thin documentary trail: advance mobilization fee exceeding 30% of total contract and paid before cargo inspection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the milestone; multi-currency escrow/counter-indemnity arrangement with the counterparty's bank; source-of-funds declaration from the client's bank officer (bank reference); copy of the client's audited financial statements; an external counsel legal opinion confirming the client's capacity; progress-bond or bank-guarantee instrument covering the advanced amount; rationale memorandum for mobilization (e.g., catapult rentals, port-crane deposits and right-of-way fees).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder injection of USD/EUR equity into the EG_LLC must route through a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank via SWIFT MT103 with a correctly declared purpose code—typically 'Investment in Share Capital of an Egyptian Company' (CBE Inward Investment Purpose Indicator / Sub-Purpose 3101-Share Capital). The remittance narrative must reference the LLC's commercial registration number and, if the capital is to be treated as foreign investment under the Investment Law, the GAFI project/service invitation number obtained before transfer. On credit, the receiving bank issues a 'Certificate of Inward Transfer' (FIAC—Foreign Investment Admission Certificate) or 'Capital Registration Certificate', which the LLC must submit to GAFI to secure Investment Law protections (free transfer of profits, capital repatriation). For supplies of capital equipment by a non-resident shareholder (in-kind contribution in the form of heavy-haul trailers, cranes, or specialized bolsters), the route diverges: a notarized Contribution Agreement plus a licensed valuation report is required, and the physical import is cleared through Egyptian Customs with the bank issuing a supplementary transfer certificate to evidence the value of in-kind paid-in capital. Operational funding below the paid-in capital threshold may be injected as shareholder loans only after the capital account is open, and must be routed with purpose code 'Intercompany Borrowing/Foreign Loan' and be reported to the CBE through the bank to avoid recharacterization as capital. All inbound wires from a non-resident shareholder beneficially owning over 25% must be accompanied by a sworn source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership declaration to pass the bank's USD-compliance check.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement rails for project-cargo operations: (i) SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for milestone disbursements to overseas vendors—heavy-lift vessel charter, container liner, trucking subcontractors, customs brokers, and port authorities—executed against a completed FX Transaction Request Form, CBE service-import purpose code, underlying invoice, contract, and the service-import declaration; funds must be remitted in the invoice currency up to the contractual limit, and any deviation above 15% triggers enhanced compliance review. (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT710) for procurement of capital heavy-haul equipment and outsourced turnkey transport operations where payment is contingent on presentation of a Clean Air or Ocean Bill of Lading together with the OOG survey and packing list; Egyptian banks issue CRC (Cash Against Documents) LCs on 100% cash cover for an unlevered LLC, or on foreign-credit lines for the parent-guaranteed structure. (iii) For intra-Egypt cash outflows, the local clearing rails are the CBE's RTGS system for EGP payments above EGP 10,000 and the Real-Time Gross Settlement via the Egyptian Banks Company for all banking payments; subcontractor reimbursements over EGP 50,000 require a tax invoice cleared against the registered VAT number. (iv) For cross-border supplier payments in USD, banks must see pro-forma invoice, registration with the Egyptian Import Registry (for goods), and, for services, a delivery confirmation (signed provider report) before release. All EGP-denominated payments to freight corporations and government-linked logistics entities must be made through the local clearing house and cannot be settled offshore.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable currency forwards with a CBE-licensed bank covering USD/EGP (up to twelve-month tenors), supported by underlying project-cargo revenue or cost exposure evidenced by a signed freight contract; forwards are documentary hedges and cannot be rolled or closed without the bank's confirmation.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) between the LLC and an authorized dealer bank, executed only for matching the notional of a contracted capital-expenditure cycle; the bank-mandated margin must be posted in the same currency of exposure.
Buying FX call/put options on USD/EGP for hedging of firm fuel, charter, and terminal cost escalation; writing options is prohibited for non-financial Egyptian corporates.

Currency swaps on the 'deliverable EGP' basis via two separate onshore spot/forward transactions—reportable to the CBE through the FX declaration system—are permissible when the LLC has both an EGP cost base (local port services, customs, stevedoring, EGP crew wages) and USD receipts.
Export/import insurance-based covers (e.g., warehouse-receipt hedges) are acceptable where they embed a CBE-approved exchange-rate cap, but must be registered as financial guarantees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; fiscal year typically ends December 31, extended to April 30 for calendar-year taxpayers; extension available upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 500 per month or part thereof, capped at EGP 2,000 for most returns; additional tax penalties and interest accrue on unpaid tax; prolonged non-compliance may lead to enforced collection and administrative measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements certified by the external auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and file maintained at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: To be approved by the General Assembly and filed with the tax return within four months after fiscal year-end; copy to be retained at the head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission exposes the company to audit triggers, penalties under Tax Procedure Law, and possible deemed assessment by ETA; delays in General Assembly approval may subject shareholders to administrative bookkeeping penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of value-added tax and withholding tax reconciliations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly VAT returns due by the end of the following month; annual reconciliation by end of January of the following year for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT filing penalty of EGP 500 per month capped at EGP 4,000 for each return; late payment interest at 2% per month plus additional penalties; willful failure may result in criminal prosecution and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Trade License (Commercial Registry) renewal and economic activity certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) / Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal of commercial registration and economic activity certificate by the anniversary of registration; exact window determined by registration date and local governorate requirements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalties and daily fines for operating without valid registration; continued default can lead to suspension of the commercial registration and administrative strike-off from the Commercial Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll and social insurance declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI / NIO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly payroll declarations by the 15th day of the following month; annual consolidated declaration within 30 days after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to 2% of contributions per month or fraction; underpayment interest and surcharges; persistent non-compliance leads to forced collection and legal action against directors

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs regardless of size are required to appoint at least one certified public accountant (CPA) firm to audit annual financial statements under Egyptian Companies Law; independent audit is mandatory for all companies, with no minimum turnover or asset exemption under the Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) as adopted by the Egyptian Financial Supervisory Authority, substantially converged with IFRS; IFRS permitted for certain entities with ETA acceptance

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Egyptian anti-money laundering law (Law No. 80 of 2002 and Cabinet Decree No. 2368 of 2020), companies must maintain up-to-date UBO registers identifying natural persons who ultimately own or control 10% or more of share capital or voting rights; annual confirmation is required at the General Assembly, and any change in shareholding must be registered with the Commercial Registry and reflected in the UBO register; failure to disclose UBO information results in fines and potential criminal liability

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,500 per year for registered office and commercial registration agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per year for a certified independent audit of a small to mid-sized logistics LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% standard corporate income tax under Law 91 of 2005, Article 49, as amended by Law 26 of 2020. Exception: Suez Canal and oil exploration/production companies remain subject to 40.55% on worldwide profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general CIT holiday applies to project-cargo logistics. Investment Law 72 of 2017 (as amended by Law 173 of 2022) grants an investment-cost deduction of 30% to 50% for qualifying new or expansion projects in target zones and accelerated depreciation rates for vehicles, cranes, and heavy transport equipment (typically 25% straight-line or 30% declining balance). Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) licensed logistics operators may access the 50% investment deduction and reduced customs duty on imported out-of-gauge (OOG) equipment. These incentives require actual capital expenditure, job creation, and substance in Egypt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 4 - Corporate Income Tax Return (Bayan 4); mandatory electronic filing through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-Tax Portal (EgyptTax, https://www.eta.gov.eg). The Transfer Pricing Disclosure Annex (TP-1) is submitted as a mandatory attachment through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return within 4 months of the fiscal year-end; quarterly provisional advance tax payments are payable during the tax year, calculated on the preceding year's assessed tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 4 must be filed within 4 calendar months after the close of the taxable year (e.g., a 31 December fiscal year-end is due by 30 April of the following year). Quarterly advance installments fall due on the 15th day of the 3rd, 6th, and 9th months of the tax year, with the final settlement due with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Tax Card number, Commercial Registration number, registered address, and fiscal year-end, matching the certificate of incorporation of the EG_LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident operating through an Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) must reference the PE registration and the home-office tax ID; a non-resident without an Egyptian PE files no Form 4, and income is subject only to Egyptian withholding tax at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal economic activity under the Egyptian tax classification; for this entity, ISIC 5229 project-cargo and out-of-gauge heavy-haul logistics, with frequency of cross-border movements and Egyptian port usage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PE is limited to site supervision and coordination, describe the limited activity; pure offshore tramping or chartering without an Egyptian PE is not reportable on Form 4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoiced consideration from project-cargo contracts, freight, heavy-lift, escort, and logistics services, less only statutory trade discounts and sales returns. All amounts in EGP, translated at the Central Bank of Egypt rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE: recognize only profits attributable to Egyptian activities under the arm's length / PE attribution rule; intercompany charges from the foreign head office must comply with Egyptian transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct haulage costs, fuel, road and escort permits, crew costs, insurance, port handling, container chassis rental, depreciation on heavy-haul assets, and general administrative expenses, supported by audited books in Egypt and valid e-invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE: head-office cost allocations are deductible only to the extent of actual, documented, arm's length charges attributable to the PE and supported by the transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 3 minus Box 4, adjusted for statutory non-deductibles: unpaid or undocumented invoices, tax penalties, 50% of entertainment expenses, excessive interest, and disguised profit distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must apply the same Egyptian adjustment rules using separate branch accounts prepared under Egyptian GAAP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses incurred in the preceding 5 tax years that have been confirmed by the ETA or audited financial statements, offset against current-year taxable income, up to the original assessed amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE losses are offset only against the same PE's Egyptian-source profits; no group relief or cross-border loss utilization is permitted for non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Taxable income subject to CIT
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 5 less Box 6; the net base before application of the 22.5% corporate income tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE: the taxable base is the profit attributable to the Egyptian PE after allowable cost allocations, taxed at 22.5% without further branch remittance tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 7 multiplied by 22.5%. No deduction is available for dividend distributions; distributed profits are separately subject to the 10% dividend withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE profits are taxed at 22.5% as a final Egyptian tax; no additional branch-profit withholding tax applies under domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Advance payments, withholding credits, and tax paid in Egypt
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for quarterly provisional installments paid during the tax year, Egyptian withholding tax suffered on interest, dividends, or service income, and any tax deposits made through the e-Tax portal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE: credit only for Egyptian taxes actually withheld or paid on Egyptian-source income; foreign tax credits are claimed in the residence jurisdiction, not on Form 4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 8 less Box 9. If net tax is payable, payment is made by direct debit on the ETA portal. Overpaid tax may be refunded upon application within 5 years of the end of the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE: settlement must be made in EGP from the Egyptian bank account; refunds require an ETA integrity review, audited financial statements, and a tax clearance certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory annex declaring all related-party transactions, the transfer pricing methods applied, and the position on thresholds; required when aggregate controlled transactions equal or exceed EGP 5,000,000, or where any related-party financing or intangible transactions exist.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annex must be signed by the Egyptian legal representative; failure to file exposes the PE and the foreign parent to the TP non-filing penalty and unilateral upward adjustment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 under Law 91/2005 Article 140. Late payment or underpayment: delay tax of 2% per month or fraction of a month on the outstanding tax due (Article 109). Knowingly false returns attract criminal tax-evasion penalties of imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years and a fine of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000 or the evaded tax if greater, plus full restoration of the tax and delay surcharges.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on gross dividend distributions by the Egyptian LLC to all shareholders, whether resident or non-resident (Law 91/2005 Article 56, as amended by Law 96 of 2015). The distributing company must deduct the withholding, remit it to the ETA within 30 days of distribution, and report it on the periodic withholding tax return (Form 41).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of its residence state for the relevant calendar year; (2) file the TRC, a beneficial ownership declaration, and the dividend payment statement through the ETA e-Tax Treaty Relief module before the distribution date; (3) obtain the ETA approval order authorizing the reduced rate. The Egyptian payer retains the approved order in the dividend register. Without prior approval, the statutory 10% is withheld and the shareholder may file a refund claim with the ETA within 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and technical/marketing fees paid to non-residents: 20% (Article 58 of Law 91/2005). Statutory withholding on interest paid to non-residents: 20% (Article 57), with a reduced 5% rate for interest on foreign loans registered with the Central Bank of Egypt where the lender is an established foreign bank and proper documentation is submitted. DTA rates typically reduce royalties and interest to 10% to 15% and require the same ETA treaty-relief protocol (TRC, beneficial ownership declaration, and prior approval order) as applicable to dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory when the aggregate value of controlled transactions with related parties exceeds EGP 15,000,000 in the tax year. Master File: required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 5,000,000,000 and the Egyptian entity exceeds the Local File threshold. TP Disclosure Annex (TP-1): filed regardless of documentation requirement when controlled transactions exceed EGP 5,000,000, or whenever any related-party financing or intangibles exist at any value. Documentation must be in Arabic or English, prepared under the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, and submitted to the ETA within 30 days of a formal request.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) - preferred for charter and freight pricing where market quotes exist
Resale Price Method - for agency-like distribution arrangements
Cost Plus Method - for haulage and logistics services controlled by the Egyptian entity
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) - most common for routine project-cargo logistics entities
Profit Split Method - for integrated or unique-risk heavy-haul arrangements
Other methods approved by the ETA where the OECD-compliant 'most appropriate method' analysis justifies deviation
